messages:
maria: Hey team — support got a request from Sales to temporarily bump a customer's rate limit for a live demo next week. They need burst capacity (≈5x) for 30 minutes, then back to normal. Can we do a safe flow for this?

sandeep: Short answer: yes, but we need controls. Current options are manual DB edits or blanket allowlist — both messy for audit and rollback.

alex: yeah manual edits cause weird token vs org ambiguity. We should scope by api_key + org_id and attach TTL.

maria: Sales wants something simple they can request and we can approve quickly. Security says we need logs and a mandatory justification field.

jamie: Product note: should show active transient elevs in Console -> Quotas so customer-facing teams can verify live state. UX: single-line grant with expiry and reason, link to audit.

luis: Security: require requester + approver, immutable audit entry, and webhook to notify sec/ops on grants above threshold. Also rate-limiter must still enforce per-tenant fairness (no global fanout).

sandeep: Proposal: new internal API POST /internal/quotas/elevations with payload { org_id, api_key, qps_delta, duration_seconds, reason, approver_id } that returns a token. Gate with RBAC. TTL enforced by scheduler that nukes grant on expiry.

ops-bot: automated-check: proposed qps_delta=5x triggers MANUAL_APPROVAL because >4x default allow.

alex: Implementation detail: enforce at the gateway token lookup layer. When grant exists, use overlay map: effective_limit = base_limit + elevation.amount. Keep metric labels: elevation_id, approver, origin to distinguish burst from baseline.

maria: What about nested grants (multiple overlapping)? We should additive cap but also a max absolute cap to avoid abuse.

sandeep: agreed. We'll set absolute cap in config: max_elevation_per_org (env var + console override for enterprise). Overlapping grants will sum but clamped to that max.

jamie: UX: Console flow for support: Request -> Required fields (duration, reason, customer contact, sales opp id) -> Approve modal for oncall/product owner -> One-click revoke. Show TTL countdown.

luis: Add an encrypted justification stored in audit log and HMAC on entries so tampering is detectable. Also exportable CSV for compliance.

alex: Quick prototype plan: implement DB table transient_elevations(id, org_id, api_key, amount, expires_at, created_by, approved_by, reason, status) + gateway check and metrics. Rollout in canary with feature flag.

sandeep: Telemetry: emit events elevation.granted, elevation.revoked, elevation.expired with tags {env, org_id, api_key_hash, approver}. Add alert if active_elevations_count > N or granted > M/day.

maria: Support ops asks: can we auto-generate a one-time demo token that encodes elevation and auto-expires? That might be simpler for sales demos.

alex: We can generate short-lived tokens scoped to a grant_id. Gateway verifies token signature + lookup. Good for demos where we don't want to mutate org-wide state.

jamie: Product decision: prefer grant-per-api_key for safety. For POC, one-time demo tokens ok if recorded. We'll draft console flows accordingly.

sandeep: Action items: 1) prototype API + DB + gateway check (alex) 2) console mockups for request/approve/revoke (jamie) 3) audit/export + security review (luis) 4) support playbook + runbook (maria)

maria: I'll queue the support playbook and a templated email for Sales.

luis: I'll schedule a short review next Tues for the security checklist.

sandeep: timeline: prototype in 1 week, internal canary after review, GA in 3 weeks if no major issues.

ops-bot: note: Please attach the support ticket id when you post PRs: #SUP-4821.

maria: thanks — I'll create the request template now and tag you all when done. :thumbsup:
